The Estate  ·  Neo-Georgian

Some houses hold history.This one shaped it.

Flemish bond brick. White portico. A circular lawn held before the entrance like a pause before a sentence.

Built 1915–16. Four columns. Original brick. The same hands that built Pinehurst.

The door has been open since 1916.

◆
The History
Walter Hines Page  ·  1855–1918

He named it Garran Hill.He never spent a night here.

He bought the land in February 1913. Named it Garran Hill. Six weeks later, Woodrow Wilson appointed him Ambassador to the Court of St. James.

He sailed for London. Into the war. The house was completed without him -- his son Ralph supervised. Leonard Tufts' craftsmen built it.

From London, through four years of war, he wrote home about one thing.

"The farm -- the farm -- the farm."

Walter Hines Page  ·  The Life and Letters of Walter H. Page, Vol. I, P. 354  ·  1923

He came home in December 1918. Carried from the train at Aberdeen -- miles from his land. He died ten days later.

"Well, Frank, I did get here after all, didn't I?"

Co-founder of Doubleday, Page & Co. Editor of The Atlantic Monthly. He nominated Woodrow Wilson for the presidency. A plaque in Westminster Abbey.

He never spent a night here.

The Library

Not original.Deliberate.

Three walls of shelving. Floor to ceiling. Rolling ladder. French doors to the grounds.

Designed in 2000 to the same standard as the 1916 house it joined.

When you stand in it, you cannot find the seam.

The Salon

Fire going.No one home yet.

Georgian carved mantel. Delft tile surround -- hand-painted, original.

The arch. The doorways. The fanlights. Specified in 1916. Still there.

The Kitchen

The kitchen was not updated.It was designed.

Reclaimed heart-pine floors -- the only room that departs from the original oak.

White cabinetry. Dark granite. Island. Four windows.

Every morning at 6:30, the deer come through.

The Dining Room

The shell cabinets were already therein 1916.

Original frontpiece. Butler's arched niche. 17 by 19 feet.

It has not been asked to be something else.

The Drawing Room

Georgian carved mantel.They made it bigger so they could dance.

The proportions were drawn by O'Shea before the first board came down. The mantel came back. The Delft tile surround -- hand-painted, each piece individual -- came back.

When you stand in this room, you cannot find the seam between 1916 and 2001.

The Powder Room

Fuchsia chinoiserie.A room that does not apologize.

The wallpaper is chinoiserie. The countertop is Tennessee marble. Gilded fixtures chosen because someone understood that a small room earns the right to be bold.

It is not a detail. It is a decision.

The Primary Suite

Custom wall panels. A fireplace.Fifteen architectural drawings survive.

Fifteen architectural drawings document every decision Thomas O'Shea made in this room alone. They transfer with the property.

The primary balcony -- 24 by 11 feet -- faces the grounds.

◆
The Staircase  ·  1916

The staircase has turnedthe same curve since 1916.

Mahogany volute. Original. The craftsmen who built this staircase also built the Carolina Hotel.

It has not been replaced. It has not been simplified. It turns now exactly as it turned the day the house opened.

The Grounds
4.15 Acres  ·  Private Grounds

The world outside these gatesdoes not exist here.

In 1916, those were saplings. Now they are a forest.

Twenty-eight irrigation zones. 130-foot well. Underground utilities throughout.

A 20-by-40 salt water pool, enclosed by a brick wall with iron gates. Restored 2022.

The Wee Cottage -- complete, self-contained -- moved to the grounds by sky crane.

Someone still puts flowers there.

Blue Fox  ·  Betty Dumaine's Irish Hunter  ·  Buried on the grounds  ·  1959–1984
The Restoration
The Restoration  ·  1999–2001

Thomas O'Shea.Fifteen drawings per room.

Architect Thomas O'Shea. General contractor Dennis Dunagan. Three years. Every detail drawn before any board came down.

The library built to match 1916. The drawing room made larger. The pool restored 2022.

The architectural drawings -- all fifteen sets -- transfer with the property.

National Register of Historic Places candidate -- Criterion B.

Preservation Easement: NC Historic Tax Credit · 25% FMV · up to $500,000.
